name: Almach
description: A star 120 parsecs away, 99 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 9640: radius 98.515 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 2986.6 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.138) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 9640: effective temperature 4302 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066)

radialVelocity.source: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry, HIP 9640: RV -11.5 +/- 0.6 km/s (quality D)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 9640: distance 120.482 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.125), at which the luminosity and radius hold

position.credit: Anderson & Francis (2012), Astronomy Letters 38, 331 (XHIP), Hipparcos astrometry

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 120 parsecs away, 99 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 2,987 times the Sun's luminosity at 4,302 K, so 98.515 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 9640: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Gamma Andromedae
quotes.card: Gamma Andromedae is a multiple star system in the northern constellation of Andromeda.
quotes.introduction: It is the third-brightest star in the constellation, after Alpheratz and Mirach.
